### The strongest current evidence

The opened TradingView report "Bitcoin Drops Below $81K, Triggering Nearly $1B Crypto Liquidation Wave: Crypto Stocks Fall With AI Infrastructure Plays" is the only article body read in this run. It carries a publication time of **2026-10-08T17:35:14Z**. ### Why one event can touch several businesses

The shared channel named in that report is financing, not chips. The report says these miners need external capital to build data center capacity, and that higher yields lower the present value of future lease income. That discount-rate channel applies to any capital-hungry data center operator, so one shock can move several unrelated businesses at once.

This is durable background, not today's driver. Zopedia page **`theme:ai-neocloud-reliability-risk`** records that ex-crypto miners face power, cooling, and neocloud execution risk. Page **`market_event_2026_09_24_semiconductor_rate_pullback`** shows the same rate sensitivity on **2026-09-24**, when the 10-year Treasury yield rose above **5.1%**. Those pages explain sensitivity. They do not prove today's cause.

### What the evidence does not support

The premise of a broad cloud and semiconductor selloff is not verified here.

- No source in this set names a shared cloud or semiconductor development on **2026-10-08**.
- The live headline set is thin. A Seeking Alpha item published **2026-10-08T14:16:52Z** states Nvidia's forward multiple is near decade lows. That is a valuation note, not a shared driver. - Zopedia page **`LITE`** shows **Lumentum closed at 1072.63 on 2026-10-08, up 12.4% from 954.62 on 2026-09-21**. That is a multi-week move, not a same-day gain, so it does not by itself contradict an October 8 selloff.
